scope: Single JSON backend required by current Schedule v1 read/v2 write evolution

paired.method: Actual fixed Source format/parser and backend versus Native, including persisted documents, no-op reads/deletes, snapshots and concurrent handle exclusion.

verification.native: 27 passed: publication failures/rollback, held writes/close and pending opens, workspace/domain lifecycle and projection persistence consumers.
verification.source: 33 original single JSON specifics and shared KV backend contract tests passed; 15 per-record tests deselected. Initial filter selected no tests, detected from JSON counts and corrected in a fresh source2 run.

behavior: Accepts explicitly compatible stored versions without modifying bytes on open. The in-memory stamp is current so the next successful atomic publication upgrades the document.
Rejects boolean/foreign version stamps and explicit null/array table shapes instead of silently discarding records.
Batch deletion publishes once, deduplicates keys and restores every removed row on failure; missing keys do not cause publication.
Unit close drains in-flight publications before releasing its slot. Backend close also awaits reserved pending opens and refuses their live results; repeated close calls await completion.

cleanup.retained: Commands, hashes, exact paired observations, logs/XML/Source counts and cleanup receipt. Synthetic files, short workspaces and isolated homes removed.

limitations: Per-record backend batch/close parity is outside this single-layout change. Required existing per-record projection consumers passed, but their whole Source conformance is not claimed.
Python coroutine admission requires scheduling, unlike eager JavaScript Promise entry; cancellation and all possible write interleavings are not certified by these finite observations.
Schedule task schema/runtime/application composition, complete regression, Portable/browser/Win7 acceptance and upstream promotion remain pending.
